_meta.what_this_is: A five-scene storyboard. 'anchor' is the Master Visual Anchor -- one style string every scene should share. 'scenes' are the shot actions. 'drift_styles' are what an author produced by retyping the style into each scene by hand: each paraphrases the same intent slightly differently, and only some spell the palette the canonical way ('teal-and-orange'). Composing with the anchor gives one consistent style; composing from the drift styles gives five slightly different looks, and a later palette change reaches only the scenes that spelled it canonically.
_meta.storyboard_is: A FIXTURE. The prompt string is the stand-in for the rendered image: if the style clauses match, the shots look like one film; if they drift, they do not. drift_styles 1 and 3 paraphrase the palette so a find-and-replace on 'teal-and-orange' misses them.
_meta.format: anchor (style string); scenes [{action}]; drift_styles [per-scene style string]

anchor: 35mm film, teal-and-orange, dusk light, shallow depth of field

scenes.action: a fishing boat leaves the harbor at dawn
the captain studies a paper map below deck
gulls circle the mast against the sky
a storm builds on the far horizon
the boat returns at night, nets full

drift_styles: shot on film, teal and orange grade, evening light, bokeh
cinematic 35mm, teal-and-orange palette, dusk, wide aperture
filmic look, cyan-amber tones, twilight, soft background
